analysis.title: The Global Week Ahead: Pay Now, Less Later (October 23, 2026)
key_insights: Scotiabank expects the Bank of Canada to hike its overnight rate by 25bps to 2.50% on Wednesday Oct 28, with a full MPR. A hike is about 85%+ priced in markets. Scotiabank argues a surprise hold would be more awkward and would damage BoC credibility.

Scotiabank's forecast embeds 100bps of BoC hikes, which it says drives inflation toward about 2.5% y/y by end-2027 and about 2.25% in 2028. It says that path is likely light if AI-driven inflation shows up in Canada.

Canadian headline CPI is 3.1% y/y, traditional core 2.1%, trimmed mean 1.8%, weighted median 1.9%. On a 3-month moving average m/m SAAR basis, total CPI is 3.6%, core 2.6%, CPIX 2.5%, CPI ex-8 2.2%, weighted median 2.7%, trimmed mean 2.6%.

The oil futures curve is the highest of any point during the Iran war, and Scotiabank says it is in the BoC's harshest oil shock scenarios. The BoC ex-energy commodity index is up 30% since early 2024 lows.

Scotiabank expects Canadian slack to disappear early in 2027. Q4 GDP is forecast at about 2%+. Even with 100bps of hikes it projects about 2.25% real growth in 2027, versus a BoC potential growth estimate of 1.3%.

Scotiabank estimates AI-driven price pressure could add about half a percentage point to Canadian inflation. Electricity (1.7% CPI weight) could add over 0.25%, water about 0.1% and computers and software about 0.1%. Colliers puts commissioned Canadian data centre capacity at 1.415 GW and planned capacity at 5.5 GW.

The Fed is expected to hold at 4.00% on Wednesday. Scotiabank notes one-eighth of consensus expects a 25bp hike, while markets price none. It estimates September core PCE at +0.4% m/m, which would be warm. Chair Warsh has declined to give forward guidance.
September nonfarm payrolls rose 29k, with August revised to 133k from 162k. Scotiabank calls the September gain the product of a dubious seasonal adjustment affecting leisure and hospitality.

The ECB is priced for no change Thursday, about three-quarters of a hike in December, and 50-75bps of hikes by next September. France's 10-year yield rose to over 5% from 3.65% at end-June, with the spread over bunds above 200bps. Italy's spread rose about 100bps.

French presidential politics add pressure: Marine Le Pen leads polls, and her budget plan would cut public spending by about 7.5 ppts of GDP to 50% by 2032 by sharply reducing France's EU contributions.
The BoJ is unanimously expected to hold Friday, with about two-thirds of a hike priced by Dec 18 after a hike on Sep 17. Strong core inflation is likely to make the tone hawkish.

The RBNZ is expected to hike 25bps Tuesday, with most of the move priced and the cumulative total since July at 75bps. Chile's central bank is expected to hold at 4.5%, Colombia's at 12.25%, and Thailand's at 1.00%.

Brazil's presidential runoff is Sunday. The real is up over 3% and the main stock index up about 9% since the Oct 4 first round. The 10-year yield is down about 50bps. The latest poll shows the race at 50-50. The author advises not fighting the short-term right-wing market bias but knowing when to sell absent proof.

British Columbia votes Saturday, with seat projections pointing to a likely Conservative majority. Israel votes Tuesday, and none of the main blocs is likely to reach 61 seats. Netanyahu's bloc is polling second.
The UK Budget is Wednesday. Fiscal headroom is estimated at £10-20 billion, down from £23.6 billion. A bank surcharge rise from 3% to as high as 8% is one possibility.
Earnings week: 168 S&P 500 firms report, including Alphabet and Microsoft on Wednesday and Amazon on Thursday. Scotiabank says these reports may be key to wavering risk appetite toward tech stocks.
US Q3 GDP is expected at 3.0% q/q SAAR on Thursday, and Canadian August GDP at +0.2% m/m on Friday.

sector_views.rationale: Scotiabank argues the biggest risk to housing is runaway inflation followed by sharp tightening, so hiking earlier is less damaging to housing than hiking later.

earnings_insights: 168 S&P 500 firms and 58 TSX firms report in the week of Oct 26. Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday and Amazon reports Thursday. No EPS or revenue figures are given.

tension_points.bull_case: Hiking now is the cheaper insurance. All inflation measures are on or above target, slack is closing, oil and commodity prices are high, and expectations are elevated.
tension_points.bear_case: Some forecasters argue the inflation is supply-driven, a hike would damage housing and demand, jobs are weak, and trade policy risk is unresolved. Scotiabank rejects each of these as a myth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A large, sustained stock market sell-off could change the picture, or a crash in energy prices.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets prefer a right-wing win after years of fiscal mismanagement. The real, stocks and bonds have rallied since the first round.
tension_points.bear_case: Bolsonaro has no real platform, his fiscal leanings are unclear, and a pledged pardon of his father raises long-term doubts.

theme_stances.key_argument: A 25bp hike now is cheaper insurance against inflation than waiting and needing larger hikes later.
theme_stances.evidence: To Hike is More Forgiving Than to Hold

theme_stances.key_argument: Data centre buildout could raise electricity, water and computer prices and add about half a point to Canadian CPI.
theme_stances.evidence: AI-driven inflation has only just begun to show up in Canada

theme_stances.key_argument: French fiscal strain and political risk are driving a bond sell-off that is spreading to Italy.
